correctness.rationale: Strict trace-of-x^(-p) convexity on the connected restricted-Laplacian cone and injectivity of the edge weights prove unrestricted unique optimum; Fourier diagonalization and a strictly decreasing root sum establish exactly one positive two-class allocation for all m>=3,p>0. Uniform cyclic Riemann-sum estimates apply at the optimized t because the zero mode proves m sqrt(t)->infinity, yielding subcritical integral convergence, the critical 2/log m coefficient, and the supercritical zeta/gamma constant. Explicit beta asymptotics give both subcritical endpoint limits. The standalone finite checker passed 1,401 diagnostic assertions; no infinite claim relies on finite testing.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General trace-inverse strict convexity applies at p=1, and Fourier dimension-dependent coherence describes scaling at fixed feedback. Neither furnishes an all-real-order unrestricted network conductance optimization, logarithmic critical coefficient, or continuous supercritical exponent. Methods are partly covered; the claimed phase law is not.

value.rationale: The spectral-order threshold p=1/2 is a natural graph spectral-density integrability boundary, not a hand-picked parameter slice. The theorem classifies all real spectral orders for a canonical two-layer network under unrestricted edge conductance design. It explains an abrupt change in limiting optimal rung budget, a logarithmic critical law and continuously varying above-critical exponents, with exact constants and limiting connection to determinant and coherence objectives. This is meaningful network-design structure beyond standard p=1,p=2 calculations.
